title: Quantum Sensing Applications in Consumer Electronics: Emerging Methods and Near-Term Use Cases
abstract: Quantum sensing is emerging as a practical means of improving sensing capabilities in consumer electronics, particularly where size, power, and noise constrain classical approaches. In this paper, we reviewed the near-term applicability of quantum sensing using a platform-and-application framework. Within this framework, we outlined the general sensing protocol and discussed the working of the four key quantum sensing platforms relevant to consumer electronics: nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, atomic vapor cells, Rydberg atomic sensors, and photonic quantum sensors. Through case studies involving navigation and positioning, healthcare and wearables, radio-frequency (RF) and wireless systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), and imaging, we examined the tangible engineering advantages offered by quantum sensing. Rather than replacing devices outright, quantum sensing is more likely to earn its place in the near-term by upgrading specific measurement components within hybrid classical-quantum systems. Right now, the clearest opportunities are in weak-field detection, compact RF reception, and sensing that remains robust in noise.
summary: This paper reviews the near-term potential of quantum sensing platforms—including NV centers, atomic vapor cells, and Rydberg atoms—for upgrading consumer electronics. It establishes a framework showing that quantum sensors will augment existing classical systems, particularly for weak-field detection and navigation in GPS-denied environments. The key takeaway is that system integration and manufacturability are more critical hurdles than achieving peak fundamental sensitivity.
main_problem: Improving sensing capabilities in consumer electronics where classical approaches are limited by size, power, and noise.
main_result: Quantum sensing is best positioned to upgrade specific measurement components within hybrid classical-quantum systems, rather than replacing entire devices.
method: The paper reviews a 'platform-and-application framework' by detailing general sensing protocols and reviewing four key quantum sensing platforms.
model_or_system: The platforms reviewed include Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, atomic vapor cells (e.g., Rb), Rydberg atomic sensors, and photonic quantum sensors. The sensing mechanism relies on coherently controlling quantum states to detect external perturbations.

figures.caption: FIGURE 1: Overview of the quantum sensing landscape for consumer electronics. The quantum-mechanical platforms couple to physical quantities such as magnetic and electric fields, time and frequency, temperature, and gravity, thereby enabling applications in navigation, healthcare, imaging and user interfaces, RF and wireless systems, and the IoT. The key takeaway is that each quantum sensing platform maps most naturally onto the application blocks that depend on the physical quantities it is most sensitive to. For a clearer overview of the generic state-preparation, signal-interaction, and readout sequence involved in a holistic quantum sensing process, refer to Fig 2.

FIGURE 2: Representative workflow for integrating a coherently controlled quantum sensor into a consumer electronics system. A. A Ramsey-type or related pulsed protocol applied to a quantum sensing platform comprises the following steps: the sensor is initialized (1), prepared in a sensitive superposition state (2), allowed to evolve during the sensing interval t (3), mapped back to the measurement basis (4), and measured repeatedly (5) to estimate the associated signal V (t).
